predecessors.name: Zirid dynasty
predecessors.text: the Zirid coast: Mahdia, Sousse and Sfax, taken in 1148; Tripoli taken in 1146

successors.name: Almohad Caliphate
successors.text: the Norman towns of coastal Ifriqiya: Gabes taken 'by force' and Mahdia 'breached' in January 1160, Tripoli recognising Almohad authority

ledger.x: 1146: Roger II's Sicilians take Tripoli, the first mainland foothold of the Norman Kingdom of Africa.
1148: Tunis pays tribute to Roger II.
22 June 1148: George of Antioch's fleet takes Mahdia, the Zirid capital.
1 July 1148: Sousse surrenders without a fight.
12 July 1148: Sfax falls after a short resistance.
1158-1159: the Norman towns of the coast are abandoned to the Almohads except Mahdia.
1159: the Almohads attack Tunis and end its tribute to Sicily.
January 1160: Mahdia falls and the Norman Kingdom of Africa ends.

wars.name: Sicilian conquest of Zirid Ifriqiya
wars.outcome: Norman victory: Tripoli 1146, then Mahdia 22 June, Sousse 1 July and Sfax 12 July 1148.

wars.name: Almohad conquest of Norman Africa
wars.outcome: Almohad victory: Tripoli lost in 1158, Mahdia under siege from late summer 1159 and breached in January 1160; a final peace with the Almohads came only in 1180.

certainty.note: A string of coastal towns, not a bordered territory: no page gives a frontier, and the Houben quote on the page calls it 'a constellation of Norman-held towns'.
